4. UNBOUNDED MEMORY: reading a whole file/object into memory without a size cap (`read_to_end`, `fs::read`, `vec![0; len]` where len comes from a manifest/size field/HTTP Content-Length or S3 object metadata).
5. Hash/signature verification: is signature verification done BEFORE using pack contents? TLS verification disabled?).
6. Panics reachable from malformed manifests/packs (`.unwrap()`, slice indexing with offsets from the file).

Report back ONLY verified findings with: absolute file path, current on-disk LINE NUMBER (confirm with grep -n), short verbatim excerpt (1-3 lines), why reachable, and a concrete malicious input description. Rank by severity. Do not write any files.

164	/// entry is where it appears" and justified it with "a broken link has no
165	/// target to leak". That is true of `NotFound` and of nothing else, and the
166	/// difference is a bypass rather than a nicety: `canonicalize` is `realpath(3)`
167	/// and is bounded by `PATH_MAX`, while the kernel's own resolution is not, so an
168	/// entry can be unresolvable HERE and perfectly readable by every later stage —
169	/// `stat`, `open`, hashing, extraction. The guard was then skipped for exactly
170	/// the entries it could not vet, which is the wrong direction for a rule whose
171	/// job is to keep `.ssh` out of a queryable index. `ELOOP` and `EACCES` land in
172	/// the same arm.
173	///
174	/// So only `NotFound` is treated as "nothing here to leak" — walkdir already
175	/// reports a dangling link through its error arm. Everything else is refused
176	/// and named in the report, because an answer that could not be computed is not
177	/// an answer of "yes".
178	fn escaped_or_hidden_target(
179	    root_canon: &Path,
180	    path: &Path,
181	) -> Result<Option<PathBuf>, SymlinkVerdict> {
182	    let real = match path.canonicalize() {
183	        Ok(real) => real,
184	        Err(e) if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => return Ok(None),
185	        Err(_) => return Err(SymlinkVerdict::Unresolvable),
186	    };
187	    let Some(rel) = real.strip_prefix(root_canon).ok() else {
188	        // Outside the root — but the hidden-name question is asked FIRST and
189	        // against the whole resolved path, because `OutsideRoot` is the only
190	        // verdict `--follow-symlinks-outside-root` waives. Returning it before
191	        // looking for a dotted component let that flag admit
192	        // `keys.txt -> ../outside/.ssh/id_rsa` unexamined, which is #438
193	        // reopened through the escape hatch built to be safe.
194	        //
195	        // Judged from where the target DIVERGES from the root, not from `/`.
196	        // Checking every component would refuse any target whose absolute path
197	        // passes through a dotted ancestor — `/home/u/.cache/...`, and every
198	        // path under a `tempfile` directory, which is named `.tmpXXXXXX`. Those
199	        // ancestors are shared with the root the operator pointed at, so they
200	        // are as consented-to as the root itself; the components BELOW the
201	        // divergence are the ones nobody asked for.
202	        let shared = root_canon
203	            .components()
204	            .zip(real.components())
205	            .take_while(|(a, b)| a == b)
206	            .count();
207	        if real
208	            .components()
209	            .skip(shared)
210	            .any(|c| is_hidden_name(c.as_os_str()))
211	        {
212	            return Err(SymlinkVerdict::HiddenOutsideRoot);
213	        }
214	        return Err(SymlinkVerdict::OutsideRoot(real));
215	    };
216	    // In-root: judge only the part below the root. A brain over a dot-named
217	    // folder still works — that exemption is the same one the walker gives the
218	    // root itself at depth 0.
219	    if rel.components().any(|c| is_hidden_name(c.as_os_str())) {
220	        return Err(SymlinkVerdict::HiddenTarget);
221	    }
222	    Ok(Some(real))
223	}

294	/// One traversal, two callers: the file inventory and (`dirs_out`) the watch
295	/// set. With `dirs_out` set, every admitted directory is collected and files are
296	/// not examined at all.
297	fn walk_impl(
298	    root: &Path,
299	    follow_symlinks: bool,
300	    allow_outside_root: bool,
301	    ignore: IgnoreOptions,
302	    mut dirs_out: Option<&mut Vec<PathBuf>>,
303	) -> Result<(Vec<FileEntry>, IgnoreReport)> {
304	    let root_canon = root
305	        .canonicalize()
306	        .with_context(|| format!("resolve root folder {}", root.display()))?;
307	    if !root_canon.is_dir() {
308	        anyhow::bail!("{} is not a directory", root_canon.display());
309	    }
310	    let mut out = Vec::new();
311	    // Shallowest depth from which the walk is inside a symlink; see the guard.
312	    let mut link_depth: Option<usize> = None;
313	    let marker_defaults = ignore.enabled && ignore.defaults;
314	    let mut stack = IgnoreStack::new(&root_canon, ignore);
315	    // Manual iteration rather than `filter_entry`, because the ignore stack has
316	    // to load a directory's ignore files *after* that directory is admitted and
317	    // *before* its children are judged. `skip_current_dir` on a just-yielded
318	    // directory prunes its contents — walkdir's own documented pattern, and the
319	    // same effect `filter_entry` had.
320	    let mut it = walkdir::WalkDir::new(&root_canon)
321	        .follow_links(follow_symlinks)
322	        .into_iter();
323	    while let Some(next) = it.next() {
324	        let entry = match next {
325	            Ok(e) => e,
326	            Err(e) => {
327	                // This message renders the offending PATH, and it goes to the
328	                // same stderr an agent parses for `xerj-progress` /
329	                // `xerj-done` records. An unreadable directory whose name
330	                // carries a newline would otherwise start a line here — the
331	                // #278 forgery, through a surface the progress module does not
332	                // own. Sanitised for the same reason and by the same rule.
333	                //
334	                // Routing this through `Progress` as well (so `--quiet` is
335	                // silent and `--progress json` stays one object per line) needs
336	                // a handle the walker does not have; that is a separate change.
337	                eprintln!(
338	                    "walk: skipping unreadable entry: {}",
339	                    crate::progress::sanitize(&e.to_string(), crate::progress::SAFE_PATH_MAX)
340	                );
341	                continue;
342	            }
343	        };
344	        let is_dir = entry.file_type().is_dir();
345	        // Retire the layers of directories this entry is no longer inside; see
346	        // `IgnoreStack::truncate_to` for why every entry needs it, not just
347	        // directories.
348	        stack.truncate_to(entry.depth());
349	        // SECURITY / hygiene: do not index hidden files or descend into hidden
350	        // directories. Without this the walker happily indexed `.env` (secrets,
351	        // API tokens), `.git`, `.ssh`, `.aws`, and other dotfiles into a
352	        // queryable brain with no per-brain authorization — a real exposure for
353	        // the "point it at my project folder" use case. A hidden directory is
354	        // pruned before descending, so `.git/` is skipped whole. The root
355	        // itself (depth 0) is exempt so a brain over a dot-named folder still
356	        // works. `--no-ignore` does NOT turn this off: it is not one of the
357	        // ignore rules, it is the main reason secrets stay out.
358	        //
359	        // The limit of that claim, stated because the rest of this file used to
360	        // assert it without one: this is a rule about NAMES and, under
361	        // `--follow-symlinks`, about where a link RESOLVES. A hard link has
362	        // neither — it is a second directory entry for the same inode, so
363	        // `ln .secretdir/k.txt notes.txt` reads the secret under a visible name
364	        // and nothing here can tell. Defending that needs `(dev, ino)` of every
365	        // hidden-rule exclusion, which a walk that prunes hidden directories
366	        // without descending does not have. `cp -al`, `rsync --link-dest` and
367	        // hard-linked package stores all produce that shape without an attacker.
368	        if entry.depth() > 0 && is_hidden_name(entry.file_name()) {
369	            stack.record_hidden(is_dir);
370	            if is_dir {
371	                it.skip_current_dir();
372	            }
373	            continue;
374	        }
375	        // The rule above judges the NAME the walk arrived by, which is the
376	        // whole rule when links are not followed. Under `--follow-symlinks` it
377	        // is not: a link is free to be called `notes.txt` and point at
378	        // `.secretdir/k.txt`, and walkdir then yields the target's contents
379	        // under the link's visible name. Both halves of the guarantee above
380	        // fail that way — the secret is indexed, and a link to a directory
381	        // outside the root drags in a tree the operator never pointed at
382	        // (`shared -> /etc` indexes `/etc/shadow` as `shared/shadow`). The
383	        // report made it worse by still saying the hidden directories were
384	        // pruned, which was true of the traversal and false of the outcome.
385	        //
386	        // So under the flag the same two questions are asked of the RESOLVED
387	        // path instead of the name. Loop-safety is walkdir's and unrelated;
388	        // this is the secret rule and the root boundary.
389	        // Resolving is only necessary once the walk has actually gone through a
390	        // link. `canonicalize` is `realpath(3)` and issues one `readlinkat` per
391	        // path component, so doing it for every entry costs 8-14 failing
392	        // syscalls per file on an ordinary tree and made the walk 4.2x slower
393	        // with 7.6x the syscalls — all of it wasted on paths where no link
394	        // exists. `link_depth` is the shallowest depth at or below which some
395	        // ancestor (or the entry itself) is a symlink; below that the walk path
396	        // and the real path cannot differ.
397	        if entry.path_is_symlink() {
398	            link_depth = Some(link_depth.map_or(entry.depth(), |d: usize| d.min(entry.depth())));
399	        } else if is_dir && link_depth.is_some_and(|d| entry.depth() <= d) {
400	            link_depth = None;
401	        }
402	        let through_link = entry.path_is_symlink() || link_depth.is_some_and(|d| entry.depth() > d);
403	        // The path every later stage should open. The guard resolves the entry
404	        // to decide on it; keeping that resolution is what stops the decision
405	        // being made about one file and the bytes being read from another.
406	        // `content.rs` hashes and `lib.rs` extracts from `FileEntry::path`
407	        // minutes after the walk on a large corpus, each a fresh `open()` that
408	        // re-follows the link — so a link re-pointed in between handed the
409	        // refused content straight into a document body. `rel` still comes from
410	        // the walk path: that is the name the operator pointed at and the
411	        // identity the index is keyed on.
412	        let mut resolved: Option<PathBuf> = None;
413	        if follow_symlinks && entry.depth() > 0 && through_link {
414	            match escaped_or_hidden_target(&root_canon, entry.path()) {
415	                Ok(real) => resolved = real,
416	                // Admitted by the waiver — but with the RESOLVED path, so the
417	                // bytes read later are the bytes that were judged. This arm was
418	                // empty, which stored the walk path and re-followed the link at
419	                // read time for everything the flag ingests.
420	                Err(SymlinkVerdict::OutsideRoot(real)) if allow_outside_root => {
421	                    resolved = Some(real);
422	                }
423	                Err(SymlinkVerdict::HiddenOutsideRoot) => {
424	                    stack.record_symlink_hidden_escape(is_dir);
425	                    if is_dir {
426	                        it.skip_current_dir();
427	                    }
428	                    continue;
429	                }
430	                Err(SymlinkVerdict::OutsideRoot(_)) => {
431	                    stack.record_symlink_escape(is_dir);
432	                    if is_dir {
433	                        it.skip_current_dir();
434	                    }
435	                    continue;
436	                }
437	                Err(SymlinkVerdict::HiddenTarget) => {
438	                    stack.record_hidden(is_dir);
439	                    if is_dir {
440	                        it.skip_current_dir();
441	                    }
442	                    continue;
443	                }
444	                Err(SymlinkVerdict::Unresolvable) => {
445	                    stack.record_symlink_unresolved(is_dir);
446	                    if is_dir {
447	                        it.skip_current_dir();
448	                    }
449	                    continue;
450	                }
451	            }
452	        }
453	        if is_dir {
454	            // The root is never judged by the rules below it: pointing
455	            // autoindex at a folder is an explicit instruction, and the note
456	            // explaining that it *would* have been ignored is on the report.
457	            if entry.depth() > 0 && stack.skip_dir(entry.path()).is_some() {
458	                it.skip_current_dir();
459	                continue;
460	            }
461	            // Marker-gated generated dirs (part of the built-in defaults, so
462	            // `--no-ignore` / `--no-default-ignores` disable it): names like
463	            // Unity's `Library/` or `Logs/` are too common for the blunt
464	            // DEFAULT_IGNORE_PATTERNS, so they are pruned only when a sibling
465	            // marker file proves the parent is that kind of project.
466	            if entry.depth() > 0 && marker_defaults {
467	                if let Some(label) = marker_generated_dir(entry.path()) {
468	                    stack.record_marker_dir(entry.path(), label);
469	                    it.skip_current_dir();
470	                    continue;
471	                }
472	            }
473	            stack.enter_dir(entry.path(), entry.depth());
474	            if let Some(dirs) = dirs_out.as_mut() {
475	                // The path the watcher must watch is the path the walk arrived
476	                // by — the same one `rel` is derived from — so a followed link
477	                // is watched where the operator pointed, not where it resolves.
478	                dirs.push(entry.path().to_path_buf());
479	            }
480	            continue;
481	        }
482	        // Watch-set mode wants directories only; a file's metadata is a syscall
483	        // per entry that nothing on this route reads.
484	        if dirs_out.is_some() {
485	            continue;
486	        }
487	        if !entry.file_type().is_file() {
488	            continue;
489	        }
490	        if stack.skip_file(entry.path()).is_some() {
491	            continue;
492	        }
493	        // Marker-gated Takeout noise (built-in defaults, so `--no-ignore` /
494	        // `--no-default-ignores` disable it). After the ignore files, and
495	        // yielding to them: a `!archive_browser.html` line in `.xerjignore`
496	        // is an explicit instruction and wins.
497	        if marker_defaults {
498	            if let Some(label) = takeout_noise(entry.path()) {
499	                if !stack.is_reincluded(entry.path(), false) {
500	                    stack.record_marker_file(label);
501	                    continue;
502	                }
503	            }
504	        }
505	        let md = match entry.metadata() {
506	            Ok(m) => m,
507	            Err(_) => continue,
508	        };
509	        let p = entry.path().to_path_buf();
510	        let rel = p
511	            .strip_prefix(&root_canon)
512	            .unwrap_or(&p)
513	            .to_string_lossy()
514	            .replace('\\', "/");
515	        let rel_id = stable_path_id(p.strip_prefix(&root_canon).unwrap_or(&p));
516	        out.push(FileEntry {
517	            path: resolved.unwrap_or(p),
518	            rel,
519	            rel_id,
520	            is_symlink: entry
521	                .path()
522	                .symlink_metadata()
523	                .is_ok_and(|m| m.file_type().is_symlink()),
524	            size: md.len(),
525	        });
526	    }
527	    // Deterministic order for clustering / naming.
528	    out.sort_by(|a, b| a.rel.cmp(&b.rel));
529	    Ok((out, stack.report))
530	}

207	    /// Read the manifest for `source`, or an empty one.

210	    /// version all yield "empty" plus a reason for the caller to print: the
211	    /// consequence is a full re-fetch, which must be explained rather than
212	    /// silently paid for.

214	        let raw = match std::fs::read(path) {
215	            Ok(raw) => raw,
216	            Err(e) if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => {
217	                return (Self::empty(source), None)

222	                    Some(format!(
223	                        "could not read {} ({e}); every object will be fetched again",
224	                        path.display()
225	                    )),

227	            }

230	            Ok(manifest) if manifest.version != MANIFEST_VERSION => (
231	                Self::empty(source),
232	                Some(format!(

234	                     fetched again",
235	                    path.display(),
236	                    manifest.version
237	                )),
238	            ),
239	            Ok(manifest) if manifest.source != source => (
240	                Self::empty(source),
241	                Some(format!(
242	                    "{} was last used for {}; every object under {source} will be fetched again",
243	                    path.display(),
244	                    manifest.source
245	                )),
246	            ),
247	            Ok(manifest) => (manifest, None),
248	            Err(e) => (
249	                Self::empty(source),
250	                Some(format!(

268	/// How long the transfer may run before the manifest is written again.
269	///
270	/// The bound this sets is *money lost to a crash*: a run killed between
271	/// checkpoints re-downloads at most the objects fetched in the last interval.
272	/// Ten seconds keeps that small while keeping the manifest rewrites (the whole
273	/// file, atomically) to a handful per minute even on a 40,000-object first run.
274	const CHECKPOINT_INTERVAL: std::time::Duration = std::time::Duration::from_secs(10);
275	
276	/// The manifest, written as the transfer proceeds instead of only at the end.
277	///
278	/// **Why this exists.** The mirror keeps the bytes of every object that
279	/// finished, but until the manifest records an object those bytes are not
280	/// trusted (`unchanged` requires a manifest record AND a mirror file at the
281	/// right size). Saving the manifest only after the last object therefore made
282	/// an aborted run cost twice: N class-B GETs for the attempt, then N again on
283	/// the next run, against a documented formula of N. Recording each object as it
284	/// lands — durably, via the same atomic replace [`ObjectManifest::save`] uses —
285	/// means a resumed run pays only for what it had not already fetched.
286	struct ManifestCheckpoint {
287	    path: PathBuf,
288	    state: std::sync::Mutex<CheckpointState>,
289	}
290	
291	struct CheckpointState {
292	    manifest: ObjectManifest,
293	    /// Records added since the last durable write.
294	    unsaved: u64,
295	    last_save: std::time::Instant,
296	}
297	
298	impl ManifestCheckpoint {
299	    fn new(path: &Path, manifest: ObjectManifest) -> Self {
300	        Self {
301	            path: path.to_path_buf(),
302	            state: std::sync::Mutex::new(CheckpointState {
303	                manifest,
304	                unsaved: 0,
305	                last_save: std::time::Instant::now(),
306	            }),
307	        }
308	    }
309	
310	    /// Record one fetched object, and write the manifest if the interval is up.
311	    ///
312	    /// A failed checkpoint write is **not** a failed run: the bytes are on disk
313	    /// and the run can finish. It is reported, because the consequence — paying
314	    /// for those GETs again — is the operator's money.
315	    fn record(&self, rel: &str, record: ObjectRecord, pr: &Progress) {
316	        let mut state = self.state.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
317	        state.manifest.objects.insert(rel.to_string(), record);
318	        state.unsaved += 1;
319	        if state.last_save.elapsed() >= CHECKPOINT_INTERVAL {
320	            let CheckpointState {
321	                manifest,
322	                unsaved,
323	                last_save,
324	            } = &mut *state;
325	            match manifest.save(&self.path) {
326	                Ok(()) => {
327	                    *unsaved = 0;
328	                    *last_save = std::time::Instant::now();
329	                }
330	                Err(e) => pr.warn(&format!(
331	                    "object source: could not checkpoint {} ({e}); a run that dies now will \
332	                     re-download what it already paid for",
333	                    self.path.display()
334	                )),
335	            }
336	        }
337	    }
338	
339	    /// Write what has been fetched so far, with a partial [`LastRun`] marked
340	    /// `aborted`, and return the error the caller was about to propagate.
341	    fn abort(&self, spent: SourceOps, report: &MaterializeReport, elapsed_ms: u64, pr: &Progress) {
342	        let mut state = self.state.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
343	        let kept = state.manifest.objects.len() as u64;
344	        state.manifest.last_run = Some(LastRun {
345	            finished: chrono::Utc::now().to_rfc3339(),
346	            aborted: true,
347	            objects_listed: report.objects_listed,
348	            objects_admitted: report.admitted,
349	            objects_downloaded: kept,
350	            bytes_downloaded: spent.bytes_read,
351	            objects_unchanged_not_downloaded: report.unchanged,
352	            objects_removed_locally: 0,
353	            list_requests_class_a: spent.list_requests,
354	            get_requests_class_b: spent.read_requests,
355	            transfer_ms: elapsed_ms,
356	        });
357	        match state.manifest.save(&self.path) {
358	            Ok(()) => pr.warn(&format!(
359	                "object source: the transfer failed; {kept} object(s) already fetched are recorded \
360	                 in {}, so a re-run pays for the rest only. This run spent {} class-A and {} \
361	                 class-B request(s)",
362	                self.path.display(),
363	                spent.list_requests,
364	                spent.read_requests
365	            )),
366	            Err(e) => pr.warn(&format!(
367	                "object source: the transfer failed AND {} could not be written ({e}); the next \
368	                 run will download every object again",
369	                self.path.display()
370	            )),
371	        }
372	    }
373	
374	    fn into_manifest(self) -> ObjectManifest {
375	        self.state
376	            .into_inner()
377	            .unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner())
378	            .manifest
379	    }
380	}

383	    /// What to record for an object whose bytes just landed.

385	        Self {
386	            change_token: entry.change_token.clone().unwrap_or_else(|| {
387	                // No token at all: record one that can never match, so the
388	                // object is fetched again next run rather than assumed fresh.
389	                format!("unversioned:{}", chrono::Utc::now().to_rfc3339())

397	                .map(str::to_string),
398	            last_modified: entry.last_modified.clone(),
399	            fetched: chrono::Utc::now().to_rfc3339(),
400	        }

416	/// Turn an `s3://`/`r2://` positional argument into a local mirror the ordinary
417	/// run can walk, or return `None` for a folder (the unchanged path).
418	///
419	/// Mutates `cfg.root` to the mirror directory. The mirror is named after the
420	/// bucket and prefix, which is also what `derive_brain_name` reads, so the
421	/// default brain for `s3://acme-docs/handbook` is `acme-docs-handbook` rather
422	/// than the name of a cache directory.
423	pub fn prepare(cfg: &mut IndexCfg) -> Result<Option<ObjectRun>> {
424	    let spec = match crate::source::parse_source(&cfg.root, cfg.endpoint_url.as_deref())? {
425	        SourceSpec::LocalDir(path) => {
426	            // Accepted-and-ignored is the failure shape this repo refuses on
427	            // purpose (#204): an operator who passes an endpoint has an object
428	            // store in mind, and running a folder scan instead is not what they
429	            // asked for.
430	            if cfg.endpoint_url.is_some() {
431	                bail!(
432	                    "--endpoint-url applies only to an s3:// or r2:// source, and {} is a folder. \
433	                     Drop the flag, or point the run at s3://<bucket>/<prefix>",
434	                    path.display()
435	                );
436	            }
437	            return Ok(None);
438	        }
439	        SourceSpec::Object(spec) => spec,
440	    };
441	    if spec.scheme == ObjectScheme::R2 && spec.endpoint.is_none() {
442	        bail!(
443	            "r2://{} needs Cloudflare's account endpoint, which has no default: pass \
444	             --endpoint-url https://<account-id>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com (or set \
445	             AWS_ENDPOINT_URL_S3). The account id is on the R2 page of the Cloudflare dashboard",
446	            spec.bucket
447	        );
448	    }
449	    let identity = spec.identity();
450	    let state_dir = cfg
451	        .state_dir
452	        .clone()
453	        .unwrap_or_else(|| crate::state::default_state_dir(&identity, &cfg.url, &cfg.prefix));
454	    let mirror = state_dir.join("object-cache").join(spec.slug());
455	    std::fs::create_dir_all(&mirror)
456	        .with_context(|| format!("create object mirror {}", mirror.display()))?;
457	    cfg.root = mirror.clone();
458	    Ok(Some(ObjectRun {
459	        spec,
460	        identity,
461	        mirror,
462	        manifest_path: state_dir.join(MANIFEST_FILE),
463	    }))
464	}

514	            self.admitted,

533	                "object source: {} object(s) had no ETag; change detection for those falls back to \

542	    /// The cost of this run, and of running it on a schedule.
543	    ///
544	    /// Printed on every object-store run because the number that matters is not
545	    /// this run's — it is what a cron entry would spend. Class-A requests are
546	    /// the scarce ones (R2 gives 1,000,000 a month free), and listing is the
547	    /// only class-A operation an autoindex run performs.
548	    ///
549	    /// Every count here is **wire attempts**: a throttled request that the
550	    /// client retried twice before it succeeded appears as three, because three
551	    /// is what the store bills. The projection multiplies whatever this run
552	    /// actually spent, so a run that hit throttling projects a higher schedule
553	    /// cost than an unthrottled one — which is the honest answer.
554	    pub fn cost_lines(&self) -> Vec<String> {
555	        let class_a = self.list_requests;
556	        let hourly = class_a.saturating_mul(720);
557	        let five_min = class_a.saturating_mul(8_640);
558	        let daily = class_a.saturating_mul(30);
559	        let pct = |n: u64| {
560	            format!(
561	                "{:.1}%",
562	                (n as f64) * 100.0 / (CLASS_A_FREE_PER_MONTH as f64)
563	            )
564	        };
565	        let mut lines = vec![
566	            format!(
567	                "object store requests this run: {class_a} LIST (class A) + {} GET (class B), {} MB \
568	                 transferred",
569	                self.read_requests,
570	                self.bytes_downloaded / (1 << 20)
571	            ),
572	            format!(
573	                "re-running this at the same size costs {class_a} class-A request(s) each time: \
574	                 {daily}/month daily ({}), {hourly}/month hourly ({}), {five_min}/month every 5 \
575	                 minutes ({}) of a 1,000,000/month free allowance",
576	                pct(daily),
577	                pct(hourly),
578	                pct(five_min)
579	            ),
580	        ];
581	        if self.retried_requests > 0 {
582	            lines.push(format!(
583	                "object store: {} of those request(s) were retries after the store failed or \
584	                 throttled an attempt — they are billed, so they are counted",
585	                self.retried_requests
586	            ));
587	        }
588	        lines
589	    }

612	/// [`materialize`] against any [`DocSource`], so the cache contract can be
613	/// tested without a network.
614	pub fn materialize_from(
615	    run: &ObjectRun,
616	    source: &dyn DocSource,
617	    pr: &Progress,
618	    scan_workers: usize,
619	    mode: MaterializeMode,
620	) -> Result<MaterializeReport> {
621	    let started = std::time::Instant::now();
622	    let mut report = MaterializeReport::default();
623	    let (manifest, reset_reason) = ObjectManifest::load(&run.manifest_path, &run.identity);
624	    if let Some(reason) = reset_reason {
625	        pr.warn(&format!("object source: {reason}"));
626	    }
627	
628	    pr.phase("list", 0, 0);
629	    let listing = source.list()?;
630	    report.objects_listed = listing.seen;
631	    for (rule, count) in &listing.skipped {
632	        *report.skipped.entry(rule.clone()).or_default() += count;
633	    }
634	
635	    // Two keys that differ only in case are one file on macOS and Windows, so
636	    // each run would overwrite the other's bytes and the index would flip
637	    // between them. Decided here, deterministically (first in sorted order
638	    // wins), rather than discovered as a corrupted mirror.
639	    let mut entries = listing.entries;
640	    entries.sort_by(|a, b| a.rel.cmp(&b.rel));
641	    let mut seen_lowercase: BTreeMap<String, String> = BTreeMap::new();
642	    let mut admitted: Vec<SourceEntry> = Vec::with_capacity(entries.len());
643	    for entry in entries {
644	        let folded = entry.rel.to_lowercase();
645	        match seen_lowercase.get(&folded) {
646	            Some(first) => {
647	                *report
648	                    .skipped
649	                    .entry(rules::CASE_COLLISION.to_string())
650	                    .or_default() += 1;
651	                pr.warn(&format!(
652	                    "object source: {} differs from {} only in case and would be the same file on \
653	                     a case-insensitive filesystem; skipping it",
654	                    crate::progress::sanitize(&entry.rel, crate::progress::SAFE_PATH_MAX),
655	                    crate::progress::sanitize(first, crate::progress::SAFE_PATH_MAX)
656	                ));
657	            }
658	            None => {
659	                seen_lowercase.insert(folded, entry.rel.clone());
660	                if entry.change_token.is_none() {
661	                    report.without_etag += 1;
662	                }
663	                admitted.push(entry);
664	            }
665	        }
666	    }
667	    report.admitted = admitted.len() as u64;
668	
669	    // Decide, per object, whether its bytes are already on disk. Two conditions,
670	    // both required: the store says the object has not changed, and the mirror
671	    // file is present at the size the store reports. The second is what makes a
672	    // half-finished earlier run self-heal instead of indexing a truncated file.
673	    let mut fetch: Vec<&SourceEntry> = Vec::new();
674	    let mut fetch_bytes = 0u64;
675	    for entry in &admitted {
676	        let recorded = manifest.objects.get(&entry.rel);
677	        let unchanged = match (recorded, entry.change_token.as_deref()) {
678	            (Some(recorded), Some(token)) => {
679	                recorded.change_token == token
680	                    && mirror_file_ready(&run.mirror, &entry.rel, entry.size)
681	            }
682	            _ => false,
683	        };
684	        if unchanged {
685	            report.unchanged += 1;
686	        } else {
687	            fetch_bytes += entry.size;
688	            fetch.push(entry);
689	        }
690	    }
691	
692	    report.pending = fetch.len() as u64;
693	    report.pending_bytes = fetch_bytes;
694	    if mode == MaterializeMode::PlanOnly {
695	        // Nothing is written: not the mirror, not the manifest. The LIST
696	        // requests are already spent and are reported.
697	        let ops = source.ops();
698	        report.list_requests = ops.list_requests;
699	        report.read_requests = ops.read_requests;
700	        report.retried_requests = ops.retried_requests;
701	        report.elapsed_ms = started.elapsed().as_millis() as u64;
702	        return Ok(report);
703	    }
704	    if !fetch.is_empty() {
705	        pr.note(&format!(
706	            "object source: fetching {} object(s), {} MB into {}",
707	            fetch.len(),
708	            fetch_bytes / (1 << 20),
709	            run.mirror.display()
710	        ));
711	    }
712	    pr.phase("fetch", fetch.len() as u64, fetch_bytes);
713	    // From here the manifest is owned by the checkpoint, which records each
714	    // object as its bytes land. An abort below therefore keeps what was paid
715	    // for instead of throwing the receipts away.
716	    let checkpoint = ManifestCheckpoint::new(&run.manifest_path, manifest);
717	    let fetched = match fetch_objects(
718	        run,
719	        source,
720	        &fetch,
721	        pr,
722	        fetch_concurrency(scan_workers),
723	        &checkpoint,
724	    ) {
725	        Ok(fetched) => fetched,
726	        Err(e) => {
727	            let spent = source.ops();
728	            report.list_requests = spent.list_requests;
729	            report.read_requests = spent.read_requests;
730	            report.retried_requests = spent.retried_requests;
731	            checkpoint.abort(spent, &report, started.elapsed().as_millis() as u64, pr);
732	            return Err(e);
733	        }
734	    };
735	    let mut manifest = checkpoint.into_manifest();
736	    let mut vanished: BTreeSet<&str> = BTreeSet::new();
737	    for outcome in &fetched {
738	        match outcome {
739	            FetchOutcome::Fetched { bytes } => {
740	                report.downloaded += 1;
741	                report.bytes_downloaded += bytes;
742	            }
743	            FetchOutcome::Vanished { rel } => {
744	                report.vanished += 1;
745	                vanished.insert(rel.as_str());
746	            }
747	        }
748	    }
749	
750	    // Reconcile the mirror with the listing. Anything local that the store no
751	    // longer has — deleted objects, keys that a rule now skips, leftovers from
752	    // an interrupted run, `.part` files — is removed, which is what makes the
753	    // existing local reconcile delete those documents from the index on this
754	    // same run. The mirror is walked rather than the manifest diffed, so a lost
755	    // manifest cannot leave a deleted object searchable forever.
756	    let keep: BTreeSet<&str> = admitted
757	        .iter()
758	        .map(|e| e.rel.as_str())
759	        .filter(|rel| !vanished.contains(rel))
760	        .collect();
761	    report.removed = prune_mirror(&run.mirror, &keep)?;
762	    manifest
763	        .objects
764	        .retain(|rel, _| keep.contains(rel.as_str()));
765	
766	    let ops = source.ops();
767	    report.list_requests = ops.list_requests;

798	/// Stream each pending object into the mirror.
799	///
800	/// A failure that is not "the object is gone" aborts the whole run. That is the
801	/// safe direction and not a convenience: materialisation happens before anything
802	/// is indexed, and skipping a failed download would present the object as
803	/// deleted to the reconcile step, which would then delete its documents because
804	/// of a transient 500.
805	fn fetch_objects(
806	    run: &ObjectRun,
807	    source: &dyn DocSource,
808	    pending: &[&SourceEntry],
809	    pr: &Progress,
810	    concurrency: usize,
811	    checkpoint: &ManifestCheckpoint,
812	) -> Result<Vec<FetchOutcome>> {
813	    if pending.is_empty() {
814	        return Ok(Vec::new());
815	    }
816	    let pool = rayon::ThreadPoolBuilder::new()
817	        .num_threads(concurrency)
818	        .thread_name(|i| format!("xerj-fetch-{i}"))
819	        .build()
820	        .context("build the object-fetch pool")?;
821	    let results: Vec<Result<FetchOutcome>> = pool.install(|| {
822	        use rayon::prelude::*;
823	        pending
824	            .par_iter()
825	            .map(|entry| {
826	                let guard = pr.file(&entry.rel, entry.size);
827	                let outcome = fetch_one(run, source, entry);
828	                drop(guard);
829	                // Recorded here, inside the pool, so the manifest knows about
830	                // an object the moment its bytes are installed — not only if
831	                // every other object also succeeds.
832	                if matches!(outcome, Ok(FetchOutcome::Fetched { .. })) {
833	                    checkpoint.record(&entry.rel, ObjectRecord::for_entry(entry), pr);
834	                }
835	                outcome
836	            })
837	            .collect()
838	    });
839	    let mut outcomes = Vec::with_capacity(results.len());
840	    let mut failure: Option<anyhow::Error> = None;
841	    for result in results {
842	        match result {
843	            Ok(outcome) => outcomes.push(outcome),
844	            // Keep the first failure and keep draining: every other object in
845	            // this batch already succeeded or failed, and the successes must
846	            // reach the caller's checkpoint either way.
847	            Err(e) => failure = failure.or(Some(e)),
848	        }
849	    }
850	    match failure {
851	        Some(e) => Err(e),
852	        None => Ok(outcomes),
853	    }
854	}

856	fn fetch_one(run: &ObjectRun, source: &dyn DocSource, entry: &SourceEntry) -> Result<FetchOutcome> {
857	    let destination = run.mirror.join(&entry.rel);
858	    if let Some(parent) = destination.parent() {
859	        std::fs::create_dir_all(parent).with_context(|| {
860	            format!(
861	                "create {} for object {}",
862	                parent.display(),
863	                crate::progress::sanitize(&entry.rel, crate::progress::SAFE_PATH_MAX)
864	            )
865	        })?;
866	    }
867	    let mut reader = match source.open(entry) {
868	        Ok(reader) => reader,
869	        Err(e) if e.downcast_ref::<MissingObject>().is_some() => {
870	            return Ok(FetchOutcome::Vanished {
871	                rel: entry.rel.clone(),
872	            })
873	        }
874	        Err(e) => return Err(e),
875	    };
876	    // A temporary beside the destination, then an atomic rename: a killed run
877	    // must never leave a half-written object looking like a whole one, because
878	    // the next run's size check would accept it.
879	    let temp = destination.with_file_name(format!(
880	        ".{}.{}.part",
881	        destination
882	            .file_name()
883	            .map(|n| n.to_string_lossy().to_string())
884	            .unwrap_or_else(|| "object".into()),
885	        std::process::id()
886	    ));
887	    let bytes = {
888	        let file =
889	            std::fs::File::create(&temp).with_context(|| format!("create {}", temp.display()))?;
890	        let mut writer = std::io::BufWriter::with_capacity(COPY_BUFFER_BYTES, file);
891	        // `io::copy` with a bounded buffer: the object is never in memory whole,
892	        // whatever its size. This is the streaming guarantee, and it is why a
893	        // 1 GB object costs a flat few hundred kilobytes of RSS.
894	        let copied = std::io::copy(&mut reader, &mut writer).with_context(|| {
895	            format!(
896	                "stream object {} into {}",
897	                crate::progress::sanitize(&entry.rel, crate::progress::SAFE_PATH_MAX),
898	                temp.display()
899	            )
900	        })?;
901	        use std::io::Write;
902	        writer.flush()?;
903	        copied
904	    };
905	    xerj_common::fsio::replace_file_durable(&temp, &destination)
906	        .with_context(|| format!("install {}", destination.display()))?;
907	    Ok(FetchOutcome::Fetched { bytes })
908	}

910	/// Delete every file under `mirror` whose relative path is not in `keep`, and
911	/// then every directory the deletions emptied. Returns how many files went.
912	fn prune_mirror(mirror: &Path, keep: &BTreeSet<&str>) -> Result<u64> {
913	    let mut removed = 0u64;
914	    let mut directories: Vec<PathBuf> = Vec::new();
915	    for entry in walkdir::WalkDir::new(mirror)
916	        .into_iter()
917	        .filter_map(|e| e.ok())
918	    {
919	        let path = entry.path();
920	        if entry.file_type().is_dir() {
921	            if path != mirror {
922	                directories.push(path.to_path_buf());
923	            }
924	            continue;
925	        }
926	        let Ok(rel) = path.strip_prefix(mirror) else {
927	            continue;
928	        };
929	        let rel = rel.to_string_lossy().replace('\\', "/");
930	        if !keep.contains(rel.as_str()) && std::fs::remove_file(path).is_ok() {
931	            removed += 1;
932	        }
933	    }
934	    // Deepest first, so a directory whose only contents were removed files goes
935	    // too. `remove_dir` on a non-empty directory fails and is ignored, which is
936	    // exactly the test for "did this become empty".
937	    directories.sort_by_key(|p| std::cmp::Reverse(p.components().count()));
938	    for directory in directories {
939	        let _ = std::fs::remove_dir(&directory);
940	    }
941	    Ok(removed)
942	}

1153	            self.retried_requests.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);

1160	/// Exponential backoff with full jitter in the lower half of the interval, so a
1161	/// fleet of runs that hit the same throttle do not resynchronise on it.
1162	fn backoff(attempt: u32) -> std::time::Duration {
1163	    let base = INITIAL_BACKOFF
1164	        .saturating_mul(1u32 << (attempt - 1).min(16))
1165	        .min(MAX_BACKOFF);
1166	    let nanos = std::time::SystemTime::now()
1167	        .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)
1168	        .map(|d| d.subsec_nanos() as u64)
1169	        .unwrap_or(0);
1170	    let frac = (nanos % 1000) as f64 / 1000.0;
1171	    base.mul_f64(0.5 + 0.5 * frac)
1172	}

1177	/// signature, a missing bucket or a denied read will be rejected identically
1178	/// forever, and retrying those spends money for nothing.
1179	fn disposition<E>(error: &aws_sdk_s3::error::SdkError<E>) -> Disposition
1180	where
1181	    E: aws_sdk_s3::error::ProvideErrorMetadata + std::error::Error + Send + Sync + 'static,
1182	{

1187	    }
1188	    match error {
1189	        SdkError::TimeoutError(_) | SdkError::DispatchFailure(_) | SdkError::ResponseError(_) => {
1190	            Disposition::Retry
1191	        }
1192	        SdkError::ServiceError(ctx) => {
1193	            let status = ctx.raw().status().as_u16();
1194	            if status >= 500 || status == 429 {
1195	                Disposition::Retry
1196	            } else {
1197	                Disposition::GiveUp
1198	            }
1199	        }
1200	        _ => Disposition::GiveUp,
1201	    }

## Checked and found NOT vulnerable (so you don't re-audit)

- **`walk.rs`**: symlinks unfollowed by default (`cli.rs:661` `follow_symlinks = false`). With the flag, `escaped_or_hidden_target` (walk.rs:178-223) canonicalizes, and the *resolved* path is stored on the `FileEntry` (walk.rs:417, 517) so later `open()`s can't be re-pointed at different bytes. Only `NotFound` maps to "nothing to leak"; every other resolution failure is refused — the historical `.ok()?` bypass is closed. The `link_depth` short-circuit (397-402) is sound for a DFS: you cannot be at depth ≤ `link_depth` while still inside the linked subtree. Residual, both self-documented: hard links are undefended (walk.rs:361-367) and there is an inherent canonicalize→open TOCTOU window.
- **`harvest/source.rs::extract_zip` (151-199)**: symlink entries skipped and counted; `sanitize_entry_path` (206-232) rejects `..`, absolute, `Prefix`, `CurDir`, `ParentDir`, `\`, `:`, NUL on every OS; the 2 GiB decompression cap uses `take()` plus a running counter of bytes actually read (source.rs:185-195), not the zip's declared size. Zip-slip is not reachable. Same code is reused for `corpus add --from <pack.zip>` (xc.rs:431).
- **`objsource.rs`**: `fetch_one` joins `entry.rel` into the mirror (objsource.rs:857), but every admitted key passed `classify_key` (source.rs:257-311) at LIST time — refusing `..`, `.`, empty components, leading `/`, `\`, control chars, >255-byte components, reserved basenames — applied to the *prefix-stripped* key. An S3 key cannot traverse the mirror. `prune_mirror` uses walkdir with `follow_links` off. LIST is page-capped (`MAX_LIST_PAGES`), GET is streamed through a bounded buffer.
- **`harvest/sign.rs`**, **`store.rs`**, **`identity.rs`**, **`normalize.rs`**: no reachable panics from malformed input — no `unwrap()` on attacker data, no slice offsets derived from file contents (`normalize.rs:275` `after[i+5..]` and `:420` `l[2..]` are both guarded by the matching prefix; `store.rs` splits filenames from the right). `httpget.rs` has bounded attempts, bounded redirects, an atomic tmp+rename, and a validating TLS client.
